exact_T3107_title: 1801 Prairie's south face from HABS photograph 1 (Harold Allen, June 1965, from the south-west): the picture ingested, its camera solved into data/reference_views/kimball_house_1801_prairie/, its match record written, and the south wall's two tall stone stacks built to it
chimneys_attribute_full_note: T-3003: the two tall stone stacks of the south wall, read off HABS photograph 1 (Harold Allen, June 1965, from the south-west) through its solved camera (data/reference_views/kimball_house_1801_prairie/habs_1965_01_southwest.json). Each rises from the main cornice over the south wall, straddling the wall line, in pale ashlar the tone of the walls (not brick), past the deck's cresting to a heavy head; the print's shafts, at x 870-945 and 1122-1190 px of the 1800 px copy, and their caps' tops (y 128 and 210 px), put the front one at u 14.45 about 1.2 m across with its cap at about 19.25 m, the rear one at u 3.2 about 1.45 m across at about 20.1 m. Those heights stand on a camera whose cornice reads low at the corner (see its solve); read against the cresting beside it, at about the same depth, the front one's cap still stands about 167 px (about 3.5 m) over the cresting's top. The Taylor print of c. 1895, the period view the phase guard prefers (T-1890), shows nothing over the deck where that cap would show from its eye: through its camera a cap at u 14.45 clears the build's deck there above about 18.0 m. So the front one is built to 18.0 m, the most the period print allows, and the 1965 height is open in both match records (a stack raised after 1895, or the deck and curb the Taylor record already reads off, T-3108/T-3109); the rear one, 20.1 m, stays hidden from that eye behind the north curb and is built as HABS reads it. T-3000: the flank's tall stone stack, read off the Taylor photograph through T-2538's camera: it rises behind the 18th Street wall at the flank section's east end, about 1.2 m across (x 475-515 px on the print), to about 16.4 m (its cap's top at y 462 px), under a heavy corbelled cap about 0.25 m proud and 0.5 m deep; its depth into the roof is not seen. The pavilion's stack the parent ticket names is not in this print: nothing rises behind the pavilion's gable, and the dark stacks at the print's right edge are 1811's. L-kimball-1801-deck-cresting-3000.

entries.what: the south wall's two tall stacks: the print's rise from the main cornice over the wall line in pale ashlar the walls' tone, the front one at about u 14.45 (shaft x 870-945 px) and the rear one at about u 3.2 (x 1122-1190); the build had one small reconstructed brick stack at u 3.0, v 10.0 (T-3107)

the front stack's height: the print's cap stands about 167 px (about 3.5 m) over the cresting beside it, its top at y 128 px; the build holds it to 18.0 m, the most the c. 1895 Taylor print allows (it shows nothing over the deck there), so its cap renders well under the print's (L-kimball-1801-south-stacks-3107)

the stacks' heads: a moulded collar (about y 200-220 px on the front one) under a stage of diamond-latticed panels about 1.5 m deep and a moulded cap, the stage about 0.15 m proud of the shaft each side; the build lays one plain cap 0.8 m deep (T-3109)

the stacks' lower stages: each shaft widens below about the curb into a broader base carried down the steep lower face to the cornice (the front one x 860-965 px below y 350); the build's shafts run straight (T-3109)

the south-west corner: a two-storey round bay (x 620-750 px) between the gabled face and the south wall, a single window a storey, under a pierced lattice balcony at the cornice (y 510-550) with a light in the roof behind it; the build's pavilion runs flat to the corner and turns it in a 0.44 m chamfer (T-3108)

the gabled pavilion's face: the print's spans x 465-620 px with its paired lights (x 487-600) and the gable's apex (x 543) on its axis, narrower than the build's 4.15 m and centred about 1 m further north (the 1911 sheet's front bulge runs v 7.1-9.3 before its corner cut); the build's pair and apex stand south of the print's (T-3108)

the south cornice: the print's runs from about y 548 at the round bay to y 655 at the south-east corner; the render's about 85 px lower at the bay and about 10 px at the corner. The camera or the corner's cornice is wrong, and the front T-3108 rebuilds decides which; the deck's cresting along the south curb renders under the print's with it
